source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 203: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 203: do not select tensor parallelism (TP) or pipeline parallelism (PP) before measuring the service. Assume the model graph, layer shapes, precision, parameter and activation memory, GPU count/type and usable HBM (GiB), interconnect topology and bandwidth, software versions, clocks, request-length and arrival distributions, concurrency, batching policy, and latency/throughput/error/quality/availability SLOs are recorded; label unknowns as estimates. Enumerate feasible TP degrees and PP stage partitions, rejecting any configuration without positive per-GPU memory headroom. Hypothesis: under a fixed workload and SLO, the configuration with the lower measured p99 end-to-end latency while meeting error, quality, and availability gates will outperform the alternative; this is falsified if its held-out p99 is not lower or any gate fails. Run randomized paired trials on identical hardware and software, with separate tuning and held-out request sets. Hold arrival rate, request mix, precision, clocks, concurrency, and batch policy constant; repeat after warm-up and report compute, collective or activation-transfer time, synchronization wait, stage imbalance, pipeline-bubble fraction, queueing, throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, quality checks, and recovery time with units and uncertainty. TP shards tensors and may reduce memory but adds frequent topology- and straggler-sensitive collectives. PP can reduce collectives but depends on balanced layer stages, activation transfers, sufficient microbatches, and incurs bubbles and queueing; batch and microbatch changes must be measured rather than assumed. Use only authorized, isolated failure/reconfiguration tests with no production impact, redacted logs, bounded load, and a tested rollback. Deploy the winner gradually and revert if held-out p99 or SLO/error/quality/availability thresholds regress, memory headroom disappears, or recovery exceeds its budget. Without measurements, conclude only that the choice is unresolved, not that TP or PP is universally better.
risks: No platform measurements, SLO thresholds, workload trace, or topology facts are supplied, so no TP/PP winner can be asserted.
Tail latency is load-, batching-, microbatch-, stage-balance-, collective-, and straggler-sensitive; paired results can still be confounded by thermal or software drift.
Failure injection and reconfiguration can disrupt service or regress state and output quality unless authorized, isolated, bounded, and reversible.
evidence_required: Per-GPU memory use and headroom by TP degree and PP partition in GiB
Topology-aware collective and activation-transfer timings plus stage-balance and bubble measurements
Randomized repeated paired trials with held-out p50/p95/p99, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, errors, quality, and availability
Authorized isolated recovery test, rollback rehearsal, and domain-expert review
